newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Earth tremor rocks east Mediterranean.
newsitem.headline: Earth tremor rocks east Mediterranean.

text.p: A powerful tremor rocked the east Mediterranean on Wednesday shaking tall buildings and sending residents running into the streets.
There were no immediate reports or injury or damage.
"All the people ran out into the streets in panic. Some were screaming and they are scared of further tremors," one witness said in northern Cyprus.
The tremor was also felt in Israel, Lebanon, Syria and Egypt.
An Egyptian seismologist from the Helwan Observatory said the epicentre was probably in the Gulf of Aqaba.
More than 500 people died and hundreds were hurt and left homeless when a strong earthquake hit Egypt in October 12, 1992. Most injuries occurred when badly constructed buildings collapsed.
In Cyprus, Wednesday's tremor lasted about a minute.
A Reuters correspondent in Tel Aviv described the tremor felt there as powerful.
"They evacuated the whole building. The floors shook," she said by mobile telephone outside the Reuters office in Tel Aviv. Palestinians in Gaza said they also felt the tremor.
